title: cancelability
name: Cancelability — Tidwell
rule: Provide a way to instantly cancel a time-consuming operation with no side effects.

citation.source: Designing Interfaces 3e ch. Doing Things — Cancelability (Tidwell, Brewer, Valencia)

pass_when: A time-consuming operation can be cancelled at once, with no side effects from the cancelled work.
fail_when: No cancel, cancel is not instant, or cancel still applies side effects.
overview: A time-consuming operation can be cancelled instantly with no side effects.
apply_when: Long-running work such as uploads, exports, or batch jobs.
not_when: Instant actions that finish before a cancel control would help.
agent_hint: Offer instant cancel on long work and roll back cancelled side effects.
description: Long operations need an escape hatch. Provide a way to cancel at once, and ensure cancelled work leaves no lingering side effects on data or state. Missing cancel, a cancel that is not instant, or a cancel that still applies changes traps people in unwanted work they cannot stop. Use this for multi-second jobs such as uploads, exports, or batch processing; skip it for actions that complete immediately where a cancel control would never be usable in time.
